review.translation: [because|0] [all|2,1] [the land|3] [that|4] [you|5] [see|6] [I will give|8] [to you|7] [and to your offspring|9] [forever|11,10].

analysis.evidence: כִּי gives the reason for the preceding command to look around. God promises to give Abram and his descendants all the land Abram sees.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew conjunction without a prefix or suffix.
Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה רֹאֶה, “all the land that you see,” כָּל marks the full extent of the land promised to Abram and his descendants.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, with הָאָרֶץ as its complement.

analysis.evidence: The clause אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה רֹאֶה identifies the land Abram can see. God promises to give that territory to Abram and his descendants.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a common noun in the singular absolute. The noun can take either gender. Here the feminine singular object suffix in אֶתְּנֶנָּה refers back to it.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces the clause אַתָּה רֹאֶה, “you see.” Its antecedent כָּל הָאָרֶץ supplies the object of רֹאֶה, yielding “all the land that you see.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה רֹאֶה, “that you see,” אַתָּה identifies Abram as the subject of the masculine singular participle רֹאֶה. The land is what he sees.
analysis.morphology: Independent second-person masculine singular personal pronoun, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל־הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה רֹאֶה, “all the land that you see,” אַתָּה identifies Abram as the one seeing, and the land is what he can see.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, used as the predicate of אַתָּה.

draft.change: Add Genesis 13:15 as an example of the existing le-dative sense of Hebrew לְ.
draft.definition: לְ marks the person to whom something is given.
draft.evidence: Genesis 13:15 places לְךָ before אֶתְּנֶנָּה, “I will give it,” and coordinates it with וּלְזַרְעֲךָ, “and to your offspring.”

analysis.evidence: In לְךָ אֶתְּנֶנָּה, “I will give it to you,” the object suffix on the verb refers to הָאָרֶץ, the land, and לְךָ identifies Abram as its recipient. The parallel וּלְזַרְעֲךָ, “and to your offspring,” names the other recipients.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition לְ with the second-person masculine singular pronominal suffix ךָ referring to Abram.
analysis.sense: Marks the recipient of a gift.

analysis.evidence: The suffix resumes the fronted object אֶת כָּל הָאָרֶץ, “all the land.” לְךָ and וּלְזַרְעֲךָ identify Abram and his offspring as the recipients, and עַד עוֹלָם specifies the duration of the grant.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, first person common singular, with a third person feminine singular object suffix referring to הָאָרֶץ.
analysis.sense: give land to someone as a possession

analysis.evidence: In לְךָ אֶתְּנֶנָּה וּלְזַרְעֲךָ, “I will give it to you and to your descendants,” the two לְ phrases identify Abram and his descendants as recipients of the land he sees. עַד עוֹלָם, “forever,” gives the duration of the promise.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ means “and,” and the preposition לְ means “to.” The masculine singular noun זֶרַע is collective and stands in construct with the second-person masculine singular suffix ךָ, “your,” referring to Abram.
analysis.sense: Abram’s descendants as recipients of the land promise

analysis.evidence: In Genesis 13:15, עַד עוֹלָם gives the duration of the land grant to Abram and his descendants. Together the words mean “forever.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition governing עוֹלָם, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The phrase עַד עוֹלָם means “forever” and specifies how long the grant of the land to Abram and his descendants will last.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, serving as the object of the preposition עַד.
analysis.sense: duration with no stated endpoint (in context)
